and the Distinguished Service Crosses of the Armed Forces and before  
the Distinguished Service Medals of the Armed Forces.
S ec. 3. No more than one Defense Distinguished Service Medal  
shall be awarded to any one person, but for each succeeding exception­
ally meritorious period of service justifying such an award, a suitable  
device may be awarded to be worn witn that Medal as prescribed by  
appropriate regulations of the Department of Defense.

awarded posthumously and, when so  
such representative of the deceased as

EO 14085 section 6 (87 FR 60541, effective on signing October 3, 2022, as the order states no other effective date) strikes military officer in section 1 and inserts member of the Armed Forces of the United States, and strikes he in section 2 and inserts the Secretary. Section 1 allows the Administrator of Veterans Affairs to authorize actual necessary travel expenses including lodging and subsistence for claimants and beneficiaries; section 2 allows a mileage allowance and ferry, bridge, road and tunnel tolls in lieu of actual expenses; section 3 extends travel expenses to a non-employee attendant; section 4 permits payment before completion of travel for listed items; section 5 authorizes implementing rules; section 6 supersedes EO 11142 of February 12, 1964 (a one-time supersession performed on September 6, 1966, whose consequence persists). EO 11429 (September 9, 1968, 33 FR 12817) changed five cents a mile to six cents a mile in the first sentence of section 2; EO 11609 section 7(b) (July 22, 1971, 36 FR 13747) replaced the words allowance of not more than six cents a mile with an allowance in such amount per mile as the Administrator shall from time to time fix pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 111 as affected by that order. Those amendments changed the mileage rule in section 2 but the clause continues, amended. Current 38 CFR part 70 lists E.O. 11302 in its authority citations and nothing held ends the clause.

such mileage allowance, the Administrator may allow reimbursement

payment and such reimbursement to the person who or the organiza­

other than an employee of the Veterans’  Administration for the per­

By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 111 of Title 38 of 
the United States Code, as amended by the Act of June 18, 1966 
(Public Law 89-455), it is hereby ordered as follows:

or approve the payment of the actual necessary expenses of travel, in­
cluding lodging and subsistence, of any claimant or beneficiary of the

istration facility, or other place, in connection with vocational reha­
bilitation or counseling, or for the purpose of examination, treatment,

or the organization which has actually paid the expenses of such travel, 
including lodging and subsistence.

approve in lieu of actual necessary expenses of travel, including 
lodging and subsistence, payment of an allowance of not more than 
five cents a mile to any claimant or beneficiary of the Veterans’  Admin­
istration traveling to or from a Veterans’  Administration facility, or 
other place, in connection with vocational rehabilitation or counseling, 
or for the purpose of examination, treatment, or care. In  addition to 
such mileage allowance, the Administrator may allow reimbursement 
for the actual, cost of ferry fares, and bridge, road, and tunnel tolls.

payment and such reimbursement to the person who or the organiza­
tion which has actually paid the expenses of such travel, including 
lodging and subsistence.

other than an employee of the Veterans’  Administration for the per­
formance of travel specified in Sections 1 and 2 hereof, the travel ex­
penses of such attendant may be allowed in the same manner and to 
the same extent that travel expenses are allowed to such claimant or 
beneficiary.

and revered American; and

Army George C. Marshall devoted his life  
to the service of his country aad to the  
advancement of the cause of peace  
throughout the world:

authority vested in me as President of  
the United States, I hereby designate the  
facilities of the National Aeronautics and  
Space Administration at Huntsville, Ala­
bama, as the George C. Marshall Space  
Flight Center; and such facilities shall  
hereafter be known and referred to by  
that name.

Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Vacancies Reform 
Act of 1998, as amended, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq. (the ‘‘Act’’), it is hereby 
ordered that: 
Section 1. Order of Succession. Subject to the provisions of section 2 of 
this order and to the limitations set forth in the Act, the following officials 
of the Department of Veterans Affairs, in the order listed, shall act as 
Secretary of Veterans Affairs (Secretary) and perform the functions and 
duties of the office of the Secretary during any period in which both the 
Secretary and the Deputy Secretary of Veterans Affairs have died, resigned, 
or otherwise become unable to perform the functions and duties of the 
office of Secretary: 
(a) Under Secretary for Health; 
(b) Under Secretary for Benefits; 
(c) Under Secretary for Memorial Affairs; 
(d) Chief of Staff; 
(e) General Counsel and Assistant Secretaries, with precedence among 
them in the order, by date, of their appointments and, if on the same 
date, in the order in which they have taken the oath of office; 
(f) Chairman, Board of Veterans’ Appeals; 
(g) Network Director, Veterans Integrated Service Network 8; 
(h) Network Director, Veterans Integrated Service Network 7; 
(i) Director, Southern Area, Veterans Benefits Administration; and 
(j) Network Director, Veterans Integrated Service Network 19. 
Sec. 2. Exceptions. (a) No individual who is serving in an office listed 
in section 1(a)–(j) of this order in an acting capacity shall, by virtue of 
so serving, act as Secretary pursuant to this order. 
(b) No individual who is serving in an office listed in section 1(a)– 
(j) of this order shall act as Secretary unless that individual is otherwise 
eligible to so serve under the Act. 
(c) Notwithstanding the provisions of this order, the President retains 
discretion, to the extent permitted by law, to depart from this order in 
designating an acting Secretary. 
Sec. 3. Revocations. (a) Executive Order 13247 of December 18, 2001, is 
hereby revoked; 
(b) Section 4(g) of Executive Order 13261 of March 19, 2002, is hereby 
revoked; 
(c) Presidential Memorandum of March 19, 2002 (Designation of Officers 
of the Department of Veterans Affairs), is hereby revoked; and 
(d) Presidential Memorandum of February 12, 2003 (Designation of Officers 
of the Department of Veterans Affairs to Act as Secretary of Veterans Affairs), 
is hereby revoked.

research_rationale:
EO 13736 (signed August 12, 2016; 81 FR 54711, Federal Register issue of August 17, 2016) provides an order of succession within the Department of Veterans Affairs under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998. I read the complete held Federal Register text: an authority paragraph; section 1 (ten listed officials, (a) to (j), who act as Secretary when both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary are unable to serve); section 2 (exceptions, (a) to (c)); section 3 (four revocations: EO 13247, section 4(g) of EO 13261, and two presidential memoranda of March 19, 2002 and February 12, 2003); section 4 (no rights created). The dossier inventory has 21 clauses, including two OCR fragments of section 2(b) (scopes sec2-b and sec2-j are the two halves of paragraph (b)); I confirmed it as the complete inventory without correction. Section 3's four revocations are self-executing and were performed when the order took effect (signed August 12, 2016; the text has no later effective date), so those four clauses are terminated by performance on that date; the surviving consequence (the revoked instruments stay revoked) is not a command of this order. All other clauses have no end date or ending condition. The held-text number search finds EO 13736 only in its own copies (the Federal Register issue and the Federal Register notice text), no held later order, statute or regulation names it, and the three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) have no hit and no disposition note. Table IV lists the order at a note to 5 U.S.C. 3345, but no printed note text exists, so I draw nothing from it. The operative clauses continue on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
